key_insight: Suboxide bonding at oxidized silicon nanowire interfaces couples tensile deformation to localized bond weakening and facet-dependent electronic responses.
engineering_relevance: Controlling interface chemistry and crystallographic facets could help tailor strain-sensitive silicon nanowires for nanoelectronic devices.
method: Simulate dry thermal oxidation using reactive force field molecular dynamics.
Track interfacial bond order, bond elongation, and stress redistribution under tensile strain.
Use density functional theory on facet-specific models to assess electronic responses.
evidence_signal: Simulations identify elongated, lower-bond-order interfacial Si–Si bonds associated with partial oxidation, localized stress, and preferential rupture, while first-principles calculations reveal facet-dependent electronic responses.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational findings without experimental validation or quantitative device-performance benchmarks.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Interfacial Bond Evolution and Facet-dependent Strain Response of Electronic Properties in Oxidized Silicon Nanowires
